question: Sapna invested ₹20,700 on simple interest, partly at 9% per annum and partly at 14% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 3 years, then find the sum invested at 9% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When simple interests from two parts of an investment are equal, the ratio of the principals is inversely proportional to their respective products of rate and time.

Ratio of investments P₁ : P₂ = (R₂ × T₂) : (R₁ × T₁)

Since the time is equal (3 years), P₁ : P₂ = 14 : 9

Sum invested at 9% (P₁) = [14 ÷ (14 + 9)] × 20700

P₁ = (14 ÷ 23) × 20700 = 14 × 900 = 12600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount invested = ₹20,700

Rate for first part (R₁) = 9% p.a., Time (T) = 3 years

Rate for second part (R₂) = 14% p.a., Time (T) = 3 years

Simple Interest from both parts is equal.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
